description: Canonical test vector for the join-date rule on a climb Ascend did not measure: leaderboards count from the day a climber joins, so a typed or imported climb that started before the account was created is history. It fills the climber's own records, streak and personal bests and never a board. The same cases pin the Swift implementation (ClimbPacePolicy.leaderboardStatus with accountCreatedAt, AscendApp/Shared/Models/ClimbPacePolicy.swift) and the TypeScript derivation (parseEligibleWorkout and startedBeforeAccount in functions/src/leaderboardStats.ts). A live climb is measured by Ascend's own sensor and can never predate the account, so it is never asked. accountCreatedAt is Firebase Auth's creation time; startedAt is the workout's start. deviceLeaderboardStatus is what ClimbPacePolicy.leaderboardStatus stores; serverCountsOnLeaderboards is whether parseEligibleWorkout derives the climb into a standing. The pace ceiling is not under test here (SharedTestVectors/climb-pace-policy-vector.json owns it), so every case is inside it.

cases.name: an imported climb from before the account is history
a typed climb dated before the account is history
a climb one second before the account is history
a climb that starts the moment the account does counts
an imported climb after the account counts
a typed climb after the account counts
a live climb is never history
